subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Box plot help: categorical variable with proportions

messages.author: 0c0915d54307a5d8
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Box plot help: categorical variable with proportions
parts:
Hi Zach,

If I understand the issue correctly, your response variable (breastfeeding status), is binomial, so you can't really take an average with upper and lower quartiles. Therefore, a boxplot would be inappropriate. If you want a bar plot, it would be pretty simple:

ggplot(bf_only2, aes(x=wk, fill = bf)) + geom_bar()

The default will stack the statuses on top of each other. If you want them side by side you can use:

ggplot(bf_only2, aes(x=wk, fill = bf)) + geom_bar(position = "dodge")

You could also calculate the proportion breast feeding at each week and create a new data frame:

library(plyr)
bf_prop = ddply(bf_only2, .(wk), summarize, prop = length(infant[which(bf=="EBF")])/length(infant))

I would actually make a line graph with proportion over time:
 ggplot(bf_prop, aes(x=wk, y=prop)) + geom_line() + ylim(0,1)

Hope that helps!
Rosie

On Thu, Mar 3, 2016 at 2:37 PM, Zachary Pierce <zspi...@ucdavis.edu> wrote:
Hi.  I'm having issues making a boxplot in ggplot.  I have breastfeeding status (EBF or NonEBF) at 5 different timepoints, and would like to create a plot that shows the proportions of bf status grouped by type at each time.  There is no response variable, i.e. the y axis will just be the frequency of observations per week.  I am not sure what I would insert in the "y" position in ggplot, as the scale is dependent on the proportions/frequencies per group.  Perhaps a bar chart would be a better option?

I'm not familiar with how to post reproducible data or use dput, so I have attached the .csv with my data. 

P.S.  wk (week) and "infant" are factors (infant isn't really needed, it's just the subject I was using for chi square analysis, or maybe it IS necessary :/ ).

Thanks in advance for all the help.

Cheers!

Zach
